citation_short: Walsh Arnold & Michaels. Effects of pollination limitation and seed predation on female reproductive success of a deceptive orchid
barrier_material: dialysis tubing secured at both ends
barrier_timing: after floral dehiscence and after initial fruit set was scored two weeks later
experimental_detail: Following floral dehiscence pollinator-exclusion bags were removed; initial fruit set was scored two weeks later; all fruits were then covered in dialysis tubing and secured at both ends to exclude insect damage.
predator_or_damage_endpoint: insect damage / weevil seed predation while fruit development and abortion were subsequently monitored
observed_method_result: Published protocol demonstrates that a porous tubing barrier can remain on developing fruits while later fruit abortion/seed outcomes are measured.
failure_mode_or_limit: Barrier was applied much later than the P. rex oviposition window, so this validates material class feasibility rather than focal timing.
pedicularis_G_relevance: Strong external material-class precedent for soft porous tubing; candidate G-A material but must be applied earlier and audited for water-y, geometry and mechanical effects in P. rex.

citation_short: Baker-Méio et al. Context-dependent benefits from ant-plant mutualism in three sympatric varieties of Chamaecrista desvauxii
barrier_timing: bags added as fruits matured; control fruits briefly sham-bagged early and later bagged for collection
experimental_detail: Seed predators were excluded by bagging each developing fruit with mesh; plants were revisited weekly so no developing fruits remained unprotected.
predator_or_damage_endpoint: fruit attack by chewing and sucking insects; fruit set and filled seeds
observed_method_result: Mesh exclusion reduced chewing-insect seed-predator access and could alter reproductive outcomes without changing early pollination rates.
failure_mode_or_limit: Very young fruits were difficult to manipulate; thin peduncles could snap under wet bag weight; sucking insects could attack through mesh holes, so exclusion was mainly effective against chewers.
pedicularis_G_relevance: Direct warning for P. rex material selection: barrier mass and aperture size are biological variables; mesh alone may fail against an ovipositor/piercing attack route.

citation_short: Menges Waller & Gawler. Seed Set and Seed Predation in Pedicularis furbishiae
barrier_material: aluminum mesh cages around groups of immature scapes
experimental_detail: Groups of 3-6 immature scapes were caged for an unrelated spittlebug experiment; cages were removed before flowering to allow pollination.
observed_method_result: Previously caged scapes later had normal seed predation, supporting the inference that the plume-moth seed predator attacked after pollination.
failure_mode_or_limit: The barrier was absent during predator attack, so it does not test exclusion effectiveness.
pedicularis_G_relevance: Within-genus temporal precedent that supports post-pollination deployment, but not material effectiveness.
